reason: Verified by driving master.html in chromium, not by reading frames. state=owner-editing (and the same moment opened by hand from owner-flight) on 'Send the invitations': at open the field reads '8 August 2026', readout 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days', row 'Sat 8 Aug', data-away 23. After +7 the readout, the row date line, data-date, data-away and the grab's accessible name all move to 15 Aug / 30 days and the undo bar says 'moved 7 days later' — and #b-edit-date still reads '8 August 2026'. After −1 everything else reads 14 Aug / 29 days; the field still reads '8 August 2026'. Undoing the −1 moves everything back to 15 Aug; the field still reads '8 August 2026'. The code confirms it: setAway() at render-b.js:550 is documented as the only writer and updates .b-away, .b-date, data-date, the grab label, .b-stepRead, the stepper disabled states and the ceiling note — it never touches #b-edit-date. Only commitDate() writes the field, so the value is frozen at whatever it was seeded with when the editor opened. This is not restating a gate: the primary-gesture block of interaction-check.mjs (lines ~330-420) asserts the count, date line, accessible name, readout and gap note all follow the move, and asserts nothing about the input's value; the typed-date block (~1035-1072) only exercises the commitDate path. Nothing in either gate can see it. It is also worse than the finding claims. The stale field is not merely cosmetic, it is a live trap: focus it after those two presses and press Enter — no typing at all — and the moment silently jumps back from 14 Aug to 8 Aug and the undo bar records 'moved 6 days earlier'. The owner's own two presses are reverted by a keystroke into a field that looks like it already agrees with them. Fixing the write closes that too. The proposed guard is correct but nearly moot as stated, and its blur half is under-specified: clicking a stepper blurs the input (activeElement becomes .b-step), and the Ctrl+Z handler at render-b.js:1009 already returns early while an INPUT is focused, so the focused-and-different case is essentially unreachable from either move path — harmless to keep, but it is not what makes the fix safe. 'Rewrite it on blur', taken literally, does make one thing worse: a refused value keeps focus with aria-invalid='true' and its reason showing ('That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026.'), and blanket-rewriting on blur would replace the owner's rejected text with the committed date while the reason still sits under it — the same contradiction one level down. Real, specific, unseen by automation, and worth fixing at a 9.5 bar with the fix sharpened.
sharpenedFix: Make setAway() the single writer of the field, exactly as it is already the single writer of every other fact. Inside setAway, after the iso is computed: var input = root.querySelector('#b-edit-date'); if (input && document.activeElement !== input) { input.value = F.fmt.medium(iso) + ' ' + F.fmt.year(iso); input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'false'); }. That one addition covers every path for free — both stepper undo closures (render-b.js:687 and the commitDate undo at :830, which can then drop its manual input.value line), and commitDate's own success write at :821, which becomes redundant and should be deleted so there is one writer, not two. Clearing aria-invalid there also fixes an adjacent existing glitch: press a stepper while a refusal is showing and the hint is cleared but the input stays aria-invalid='true' under text the panel no longer objects to. Do NOT add a blanket blur rewrite. The change event already fires before blur and commits, so blur needs no help on the success path; on the refusal path the field must keep the text the owner typed next to the reason it was refused, so if a blur rewrite is added at all it must be skipped whenever aria-invalid is 'true'. Then add two assertions to interaction-check.mjs's primary-gesture block, since this is precisely the drift the gate was built to catch: after a stepper press #b-edit-date.value === FIXTURE.fmt.medium(after.date) + ' ' + FIXTURE.fmt.year(after.date), and the same after Undo — plus one that focusing the field and pressing Enter with no typing leaves data-away unchanged and adds no history entry.
